/cards/20/segments/0/text: One morning two boys were found in the basket for abandoned infants at the door. Before the wet-nurse arrived, they already had names: {{e_manuel|Manuel}} and {{e_esteban|Esteban}}. The names were distinct; the children were not. No one in the city could reliably tell which was which.
/cards/20/segments/1/text: No one knew their parents. Later, seeing how straight they stood and how silent they were, the city's gossips invented distinguished origins for them, assigning them to one noble doorway after another. None of these stories restored a family to them or spared them any teasing as they grew.
/cards/20/segments/2/text: [[NPC1]] was the nearest thing they had to a guardian. She often hated the suffering men brought upon women, yet gradually grew fond of these two children. In the evenings she called them into her room, sent to the kitchen for cakes, and told stories of heroes and the successive misfortunes of a clown.
/cards/20/segments/3/text: Two pairs of dark eyes watched her intently. The more she loved them, the more abruptly she would worry: when they became men, would the things she hated emerge from these faces too? The boys did not understand the hesitation in her gaze. They waited for the story to continue.
/cards/20/segments/4/text: They remained until they were a little too old to stay, then worked in churches throughout the city: mending hedges, polishing crucifixes, carrying the censer behind priests entering sickrooms. Everyone knew the brothers, and still confused their names. Later they became copyists. With their similar hands they transcribed plays, ballads, merchants' notices and endless parts for the choirs. They had possessed names from the beginning. Only each brother could recognise the other without needing one.
/cards/21/segments/0/text: When she reached the part where they nailed the man up, I interrupted. If {{e_esteban|Esteban}} and I had been there, we would have stopped them. It did not sound like a boast when I said it. Two people could surely do something. How could they simply stand and watch?
/cards/21/segments/1/text: {{e_abbess|Mother Pilar}} looked at us for a while. Her stories of distant places often contained people suffering, or people who arrived too late. I disliked hearing 'too late'. When we ran errands for her, a blocked road meant finding another. If something was heavy, we each took one end.
/cards/21/segments/2/text: People in the city confuse us, then laugh at their own mistake. I do not want to explain so much. In this room at {{e_convent|Saint Rose's Convent}}, we can sit beside one another, listen quietly, and speak when we wish.
/cards/21/segments/3/text: Had we been there, we would have changed it. When I said that, I had never yet met a thing that had to be done and could not be done, however hard one tried.
/cards/22/segments/0/text: The {{e_archbishop|Archbishop of Lima}} heard that the twins spoke a language only they understood. He trimmed a quill and summoned them to his study. He had studied dialects and hoped to make an interesting project of these materials when he returned to his estate in Spain.
/cards/22/segments/1/text: How do you say bread? When you are alone together, what word do you use?
/cards/22/segments/2/text: {{e_manuel|Manuel}} and {{e_esteban|Esteban}} stood upon the fine carpet. After a long silence one of them answered softly. Their questioner moved his pen towards the paper.
/cards/22/segments/3/text: And a tree? Do you have a word for a tree as well? Do not be troubled. Just say what you ordinarily say.
/cards/22/segments/4/text: Another silence. They had possessed this {{e_language|Private Language}} since learning to speak; its vocabulary and syntax owed little to Spanish. They used it when alone. On the rare urgent occasion before others, they whispered.
/cards/22/segments/5/text: Then would 'I see' differ from 'I have seen'? Slowly, please, so that I can write it down.

Strangers usually found amusement in staring at their similar faces. Now, question by question, even the most private space between them was being laid upon the desk.
/cards/22/segments/7/text: At first their host thought the splendour of his study had restrained them. Eventually he perceived that their hesitation came from somewhere deeper. Disappointed, he put down the quill and dismissed them without asking for another word. The language remained between the brothers. The notebook held far less than he had expected.
/cards/23/segments/0/text: People ask why we take different streets even when going on the same errand. It saves us hearing them guess who is who. They laugh when they are right and when they are wrong. Whatever we answer, we have to stand there until they have finished.
/cards/23/segments/1/text: {{e_esteban|Esteban}} need not tell me when he will return. Sometimes, at my work, I feel he is almost here. A little later there are footsteps outside. If others heard that, they would probably ask many questions. We are used to it. We do not feel obliged to explain.
/cards/23/segments/2/text: When we tire of copying, we carry cargo at the {{e_harbor|Harbour}}. We have driven animals, picked fruit, ferried people across water. Different work makes different parts of the back ache. At home there is still someone who knows why I am quiet that day.
/cards/23/segments/3/text: We seldom discuss anything grand. Food, clothing, where to earn tomorrow's money: a few words suffice. Whether it is two desks or a heavy wooden crate, I know someone is on the other side. However noisy the rest of the world becomes, I need not understand it immediately.
/cards/24/segments/0/text: The manager expected empty seats that evening and gave the brothers two tickets. Since returning to the city they had resumed copying for the company. They went backstage regularly, without finding much to admire in the speeches. Honour, fame, the flames of love: once a poet began, everything could be made to circle those subjects for a very long time.
/cards/24/segments/1/text: They sat patiently, watching the candles and splendid clothes. During the interval {{e_camila|Camila}} shed her dramatic role and came out to dance in layered skirts. {{e_esteban|Esteban}} said he had copying to finish and went home. [[NPC1]] remained. The red stockings and shoes never entirely left his thoughts.
/cards/24/segments/2/text: They had seen the actress before. Years earlier she had brought them together, inspected their faces carefully, then clapped one on the shoulder and announced that she had found the younger. The embarrassment of that inspection had long sunk beneath other memories. Now one brother found that almost every errand somehow led him towards her house.
/cards/24/segments/3/text: At night he stood among the trees beneath her dressing-room window, his knuckles against his mouth, listening to his heartbeat. She was the mistress of {{e_viceroy|Viceroy Andrés}}: rich, beautiful and sharp-tongued. Almost nothing he knew of her offered hope. None of it persuaded him to go home.
/cards/24/segments/4/text: His brother waiting in their room also bit his knuckles. He had not fallen in love with the actress. He could not understand why two people, who had always been enough, should suddenly no longer suffice. For the first time the same silence concealed two things they could not immediately understand in each other.
/cards/25/segments/0/text: At the {{e_theatre|Theatre}}, {{e_camila|Camila}} said I seemed not to like her. I did not know how to answer like a friend without betraying my delight at being there. I said, 'Yes, señora.' She called me stupid. When I said it again, she threatened to find someone else.
/cards/25/segments/1/text: She made me swear that even {{e_esteban|Esteban}} must not know. I kept a secret between us, only to receive words for other men. The letter to {{e_viceroy|Viceroy Andrés}} rebuked his suspicions and returned his presents. The one to the bullfighter became an affectionate arrangement.
/cards/25/segments/2/text: The quill did not stop. She told me to take another sheet, and I took one. Not a sentence in these {{e_secretletters|Secret Letters}} was addressed to me. Yet she stood so near that I felt, if I wrote clearly enough, I might stay a little longer.
/cards/25/segments/3/text: She asked whether I had copied it correctly and paid me. {{e_pio|Pio}} usually wrote for her, she said, but she did not want him to know of these letters. I took the money, went downstairs and stood beneath the trees. The words I had been obliged to hear so precisely now crowded my heart. I could not find a single word of my own.
/cards/26/segments/0/text: There was a light knock. [[NPC2]] rose to open the door, and a veiled woman hurried in, asking first for ink and paper. [[NPC3]] was already in bed, watching from beneath the covers. The visitor noticed his eyes, apologised hastily for coming so late, and leaned over the table.
/cards/26/segments/1/text: [[NPC1]] was writing to the bullfighter who had kept her waiting. Close to the copyist's ear she dictated angry sentences in a low voice and kept asking whether he had finished. She needed a {{e_secretletters|Secret Letter}} sent at once. The other man in the shadows mistook her proximity for something permitted only between lovers.
/cards/26/segments/2/text: He turned his face to the wall. The actress took the paper, pushed a {{e_coin|Coin}} across the table and departed with her black lace and hurried whispers. When the door shut, the copyist sat down, elbows on his knees and hands over his ears, admitting over and over to himself that he loved her.
/cards/26/segments/3/text: Then he sensed another silence in the room. It was as though his brother had already gone far away and was repeatedly saying goodbye. He could not understand why loving one person should cause another such pain. Still less could he understand whether a single decision could truly end it.
/cards/26/segments/4/text: Candlelight fell upon two identical faces without revealing a common thought. The money remained on the table. Already the man beside the bed was eager to prove that he still placed his brother before everything else. He blew out the candle, lay down and announced, with excessive casualness, that he would never write for that woman again.
/cards/27/segments/0/text: After announcing that he would write no more letters, [[NPC1]] began his evening prayers, hoping the matter would pass. [[NPC2]] got up, lit the candle again and fastened his belt.

/cards/27/segments/4/text: You love her. You need not change because of me.
/cards/27/segments/5/text: Love her? What chance have I? If there were any chance, would she ask me to write these letters? Would she push a coin across the table every time?

At midnight they remembered a barber's sign advertising surgery. [[NPC2]] ran to knock at his door. The man had not returned; they must wait until morning.
/cards/28/segments/1/text: They assured each other that all would be well once he had been seen. A day or two—perhaps less than a day—and the injured man would be out again. At last came {{e_medicine|Medicines}} and plasters, with one clear instruction: apply cold wet cloths to the leg every hour.
/cards/28/segments/2/text: The carer obeyed, but the patient grew worse. Each application of the {{e_cloth|Wet Cloth}} brought the most unbearable moment. He begged his brother to stop, saying the pain had gone and there was no need. Afraid that yielding would delay recovery, the other lifted the covers and pressed the cloth firmly into place. The city's clocks struck the hours so sweetly outside. Inside, the sound became more dreadful.

His carer retreated outside and leaned against the door, struggling to breathe in his shock. After a while he still had to go in and perform the next duty.
